Sophie — thanks for the RFP excerpt. High level answer first, then a short plan:

High-level sequencing (common approach we use):
1) Evaluation phase (POC / pilot) — runs in parallel with initial security intake.
2) MSA signature — we prefer to lock commercial terms and core liability language up front.
3) DPA negotiation — run in parallel with MSA redlines where possible; many customers sign DPA alongside or immediately after MSA signature.
4) Order Form (pricing & quantities) — generally finalized after MSA terms are agreed and pricing is confirmed; we use the order form to bind term, SKU and billing cadence.

Gating items to flag:
- SOC 2 report and evidence (we provide a snapshot and can provide an auditor letter).
- Data residency / private deployment options (we can provide VPC/on-prem options for EU residency).
- Procurement-specific clauses (PO terms, PO numbers, payment terms) — these are often handled in the order form.

Proposed short MAP (we'll turn this into a shared sheet):
- Week 1 (evaluation kickoff): access + test data, POC success criteria (owner: Customer PM)
- Week 1–2 (security intake): complete vendor questionnaire, provide SOC 2 artifacts (owner: Redwood Security)
- Week 2 (commercial alignment): pricing and order form draft (owner: Redwood Sales)
- Week 3 (legal redlines): MSA redline exchange (owner: HelioMed Legal / Redwood Legal)
- Week 4 (finalize DPA + Order Form): sign MSA and DPA or provide EOT (owner: Legal + Procurement)

I'll attach a MAP draft and a close-timeline sketch. Quick asks for you: can you confirm procurement's target signature date and whether EU data residency is mandatory for this pilot? That will change sequencing.

Thanks — Mateo
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Detailed sequencing & notes (proposed):
- Day 0: Kickoff call (eval success criteria, data residency scope) — owner: HelioMed PM + Mateo (Redwood SE)
- Days 1–10: Evaluation window (data scoped to EU region) + Redwood provides SOC 2 Type II summary and privacy whitepaper — owner: Redwood Security (Neha)

- SOC 2: we will provide an audited report and a short attestation letter; if additional evidence is requested we can provide auditor point-of-contact for expedited review.
- DPA: for speed, suggest HelioMed review our standard DPA and flag only non-negotiables (data deletion, subprocessor list). We can accept a DAS or provide a minimal side letter for unique clauses.
